description_en: The monument is located on a hill overlooking the confluence of the Um Kholā coming from the north, and the Tilā Nadī, coming from the east. It is found directly to the south of the village of Bayalkāṭiyā and west of Śrī Ḍhuskā.The pavilion (baiṭhak) is a unique construction for the whole of the Karnali region. In west Nepal, pavilions are only met in the district of Dadeldhura, where they can be dated from the 14th-15th century. Nevertheless, the monument of Bayalkāṭiyā shows numerous architectural differences in comparison to the Dadeldhura pavilions. It is built on a large square platform. Instead of having a corbelled dome supported by identical pillars, the corbelled dome of Bayalkāṭiyā is supported by four L-shaped blocks of stone masonry. Two of these blocks (in the southern and western corners) are supplemented with 'tablets' that could have been used as seats. A pillar is placed between each of these blocks and a group of four additional pillars are placed in the inner space. The monument is richly decorated with carvings of flower motifs (puṣparatna) and losanges (ratna). A bas-relief of Gaṇeśa (two, a not four-armed, as indicated inSharma 1972: 27) is placed on the western capital of the southern block. Prayag Raj Sharma indicates that the god is four-armedThe exact purpose of this pavilion remains uncertain as the height of the ceiling does not allow for many activities to take place (the pillars do not exceed 120 cm in height). It may be suggested that the construction was used as a meeting pavilion (sabhamaṇḍapa) or even as a pavilion of justice (nyāyamaṇḍapa) (Andolfatto 2019: 92-93).A stone memorial pillar (JUM0100-001) is erected on the north-eastern side of the pavilion.There are no inscriptions at the site. Despite this, it is possible to propose that thebaiṭhakwas erected around the 14th-16th century. This is infered by the carved motifs, similar to those seen on memorial pillars from the second half of the 14th century to the early 16th century (Andolfatto 2019,Ibid.).In a dire need for restauration, the pavilion was finally stabilised and restored by the Department of Archaeology in 2015 or 2016, after French-Swiss archaeologist Dominique Baudais provided a detailed documentation of the monument to the institution.
description_ne: जुम्लाको उपल्लो डाँडामा अवस्थित यस शिलासत्तल र स्तम्भ बयल्काठिया गाउँको दक्षिण र श्री ढुस्काको पश्चिममा पर्छ । उत्तरबाट बग्ने उमखोला र पूर्वबाट बग्ने तिला नदीको दोभानको माथिपट्टि यो डाँडा अवस्थित छ ।स्थानियरूपमा 'बैठक' भनिने यो स्मारक सत्तलको स्वरूपमा रहेको छ । यसलाई कर्णाली क्षेत्रकै एक मौलिक संरचना मान्न सकिन्छ । पश्चिम नेपालमा यस्ता ढुंगे सत्तलहरू डडेलधुरा जिल्लामा मात्र देख्न सकिन्छ । त्यहाँका सत्तलहरू १४-१५औं शताव्दीतिर बनेका हुन् । तर वास्तुकलाका दृष्टिकोणले बयल्काठियाको यो ढुंगे सत्तल डडेलधुराका सत्तलहरू भन्दा धेरै किसिमले फरक छ । ठूलो चारकुने पेटीमाथि बनाइएको बयल्काठियाको सत्तलमा समान आकारका थामहरूको सट्टा L आकारको ढुंगाका ब्लकहरूले माथिल्लो भागको भार थामेको छ । सत्तलका ढुंगाहरूमा कलात्मक रूपमा फूल र रत्न बुट्टा कुँदिएका छन् । दक्षिणतिरको एक ढुंगामा दुई हात सहितको गणेशको आकृति कुँदिएको छ । प्रयागराज शर्माले चार हात भएको उल्लेख गरेका छन् (Sharma 1972: 27) ।यो सत्तल कुन प्रयोजनको लागि बनाइयो भन्ने अझै स्पष्ट छैन । होचो संरचना भएका कारण यहाँ कुनै गतिविधि गर्न सहज हुनेछैन । थामहरूको उँचाइ १२० से.मी.भन्दा बढी छैन । सम्भवत: सभा गर्नका लागि सभामण्डप वा न्याय सम्पादनका लागि न्यायमण्डपका रूपमा बनाइएको हुनसक्छ (Andolfatto 2019: 92-93) ।यस सत्तलको उत्तरपूर्वतिर एक शिलास्तम्भ (JUM0100-001) पनि ठड्याइएको छ ।यहाँ कुनै अभिलेख देखिदैन । तर यसमा कुँदिएका बुट्टाहरूका आधारमा यो 'बैठक' १४ औं-१६ औं शताव्दीतिर बनेको अनुमान गर्न सकिन्छ । ती बुट्टाहरू १४ औं-१६ औं शताव्दीका शिलास्तम्भहरूका बुट्टाहरूसंग मेल खान्छ (Andolfatto 2019,Ibid.) ।भग्न अवस्थामा रहेको यस सत्तलको अवस्थाका बारेमा फ्रेन्च-स्वीस पुरातत्त्वविद् Dominique Baudais ले विस्तृत अध्ययन प्रतिवेदन तयार गरि बुझाएपछि पुरातत्त्व विभागले सन् २०१५-२०१६ तिर यसको जिर्णोद्धार गरेको थियो ।
references: REFERENCES Andolfatto, D. C. 2019. Le Pays aux Cent-Vingt-Cinq-Mille Montagnes. Etude Archéologique du Bassin de la Karnali (Népal) entre le XIIe et le XVIe siècle . Paris: Sorbonne Université. Sharma, P. R. 1972. Preliminary Study of the Art and Architecture of the Karnali Basin, West Nepal. Paris: CNRS.
